lines.en: What separates science from opinion is the willingness to say 'we do not know yet'.
It is a strength, not a weakness, that every scientific claim carries its own margin of doubt.
Were the universe perfectly predictable, there would be no science left to do.
However elegant a theory may be, nature has no obligation to be elegant.
Not until we admit the limits of our knowledge does real learning begin.
The map, as the old saying goes, is not the territory; a model is not the world itself.
It is estimated that we understand less than five percent of the universe we live in.
What the experiment ruled out was not the theory itself, but one of its many possible versions.
Little does the public hear about the hundred failed attempts behind every successful result.
Rarely is 'the science says' the end of a conversation; it should be the beginning of a better one.
What the scientist admits at the conference and what the press release claims are often two different findings.
It is precisely because every result may be wrong that science, unlike certainty, moves forward.
Were we to fund only research with guaranteed results, we would fund no real research at all.
Not until a theory makes a prediction that could prove it wrong does it deserve the name of science.
However impressive the machinery, a measurement is only as honest as the person reading it.
